REFUTED on two independent grounds. Verification script: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/verify/verify_lexi_universe_docstring.py

(1) OUT OF SCOPE — no number or conclusion changes. The finding is documentation-only: the implementation at partura/ops_ext.py:319-325 is deterministic and self-consistent, and the reporter's own suggested fix is "add one explicit sentence to _lexi's docstring". The "failure scenario" does not compare the kernel against a correct answer; it compares it against a hypothetical alternative implementation the reporter invented ("x ranked over all x-finite stocks"). Nothing in Partura's selection pipeline (books.py, the signal = direction x panel -> causal EMA path) reads a docstring, so no long-book membership, Sharpe or holdout number moves. The brief explicitly excludes comments/docs from reportable defects.

(2) THE PREMISE IS FALSE — the universe IS determined, because the reporter's "equally literal" alternative contradicts three EXPLICIT sentences of the same cs_first_low40 docstring that low20/high20/high40/low40 defer to. Reproduced:
  - I confirmed the reporter's arithmetic (kernel = [1.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.0, nan]; alternative = [0.2, 0.4, ...]), so the two readings do differ. But in the reporter's OWN example the alternative promotes NOBODY, making cs_first_low20 bit-identical to plain rank(y) ("alternative output == plain rank(y) ? True"). The docstring's stated purpose is "'Trade y only where x is low' as an expression" — the alternative deletes the operator's entire effect.
  - Docstring: "the top of the output is drawn from the low-x segment, ordered by y". Implementation top-of-book = stock0, x=2, the LOWEST x of the 5 stocks that receive an output. Alternative top-of-book = stock4, x=6, the HIGHEST x of those 5 — the exact opposite of what is documented.
  - Docstring: "every stock in the LOWEST 40% of x". On a 400d x 300-stock panel with y missing on ~50% of the lowest-x names, the implementation promotes 19.84% (low20) / 39.85% (low40) of the stocks that actually receive an output — matching the documented 20%/40%. The alternative promotes 11.31% / 31.47% — systematically under-filled, i.e. it would make the documented percentage wrong.
  - The reporter's reading is also internally asymmetric: _lexi computes ry = _pct_rank(y, ok) over the SAME ok set, and the reporter leaves y on ok while moving only x. The docstring's uniform phrasing ("Rank of y ... every stock in the LOWEST 40% of x"), plus its promise "every stock keeps a distinct value (no NaN, no ties)" and rank in (0,1] (verified: output support is 5/5 distinct over (0,1]+shift), can only hold when the denominator is the set of stocks that actually get an output — i.e. the joint-finite set.
  - The convention is stated module-wide and by siblings: ops_ext.py header "NaN = missing; a kernel never invents a value for a missing input"; cs_bucket_rank "deciles of x by rank; NaN where either is missing"; cs_bucket_demean "NaN where either is missing or the bucket has fewer than 2 names". Every joint-ok binary cs kernel in the module uses ok = isfinite(y) & isfinite(x) (lines 127, 241, 322, 412, 428); the remaining arity=2 cs kernels are the thin wrappers that delegate to those helpers.
  - The one docstring clause that might look like support, "so the book is still measured against the whole market", is about the Partura excess 口径 (excess vs the equal-weight of all stocks with signal and label), not the rank universe; the NaN set is identical under both readings, so it is unaffected.

Since the kernel's behaviour is the only one consistent with its documented guarantees, I reproduced the output but it is not an erroneous output — confirmed_by_reproduction stays false. No file under /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura or /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube was modified; the only file written is the scratch script above.
